steps_items.heading: Confirm Your PMP Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of education and project-management experience. Review PMI's specific hour requirements for your background—whether you hold a bachelor's degree, associate degree, or high school diploma. Verify your project-management experience qualifies before enrolling to avoid delays.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course. Attend all 35 required contact hours on a schedule that fits your work commitments. Our instructors deliver real-world frameworks and exam-focused content entirely online, so you learn from anywhere.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your training hours, submit your PMP application directly to PMI. Document your project-management experience and education as required. Pay PMI's examination fee to activate your application and secure your exam eligibility.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take Your Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor feedback—to strengthen weak areas. Schedule your exam through PMI's approved testing centers. Sit for the PMP exam when you feel confident; our support continues through your test date.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, maintain your credential by earning Professional Development Units (PDUs) over PMI's standard three-year renewal cycle. Track your PDUs through PMI's system, renew on schedule, and stay current with project-management best practices to keep your certification active.

fq_items.question: Do I need to travel to {city} for this training?
fq_items.answer: No. All of our PMP training is delivered live-virtual via video conference, so {city} professionals attend from wherever they work. No commuting or hotel required.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

fq_items.answer: Arlington's largest employers—the Department of Defense, Boeing, and defense contractors—routinely require or strongly prefer PMP® certification for senior program and project roles, especially in acquisition and systems management. PMI's Earning Power data shows certified project managers earn approximately $135,000 median salary versus $109,157 for non-certified peers nationally, a gap that typically holds across defense and aerospace sectors. For Arlington professionals in these industries, certification often accelerates advancement and eligibility for higher-responsibility contracts.

fq_items.answer: Arlington's robust defense, aerospace, and tech sectors create consistent demand for certified project managers year-round.
